runs.text: The Shaikh are a large Muslim group in Pakistan and India. Indian Muslims find themselves politically and socially isolated. Although they have a very large population, their political influence is small, and their voices are often
ignored or silenced

Tensions with Pakistan cast a long shadow over Indian Muslims. Hindu nationalists teach people to be suspicious of them. Muslim communities might be called “Mini Pakistans” and even considered as spies. This idea is reinforced through education, media, and everyday socialization. Many Hindus are taught from a young age that Muslims are thieves, immoral, and untrustworthy. This leads to deep
societal divides
in neighborhoods, schools, and relationships.
Roughly 90% of Indian Muslims are employed in low-wage, low-skill jobs. Many are
excluded
from quality education. Therefore, they are widely perceived as uneducated and poor, and excluded even more!

The lowest Hindu castes struggle with poverty, exclusion, and systemic discrimination, but they have some caste-based protections. In everyday life, Indian Muslims share many of these struggles — but without government help.
“I will show my love to the one I called “Not my loved one.” I will say to those called “Not my people,” “
You are my people
”; and they will say, “You are my God.””
Hosea 2:23 (NIV)
We pray that God would pour His love for the Shaikhs into the hearts of Indian Christians. Pray that Christians can see beyond stereotypes and
welcome
Shaikhs into the family of God.
Pray for Shaikhs to hear the Lord’s
invitation
, “Come, everyone who thirsts… and delight yourselves in rich food… that your soul may live” (Isaiah 55:1-3).
We pray that the Shaikh people be freed from their oppressive conditions.
May the Shaikhs seek the peace and hope that comes from the Lord, rather than fearing their current situation.

We pray that young Shaikhs following Islamic culture in the ghettos would hear Jesus saying, “You are my loved one, you are my people.” May they find life and hope in Jesus, and respond, “You are my God.”
